21. a) Robert Szyba 
b) 1427 West Goldcrest Avenue
c) Private Citizen
d) 96
e) Questioned whether the cost of the freeway and its relation to the time saved has been weighed against the social cost of building the freeway. Questioned the validity of the noise analysis in the Draft EIS because the airlines were on strike and the east-west runway was shut down for resurfacing when the noise measurement were taken.
f) Construction of the Airport Spur can at best save only a few minutes in reaching the airport. The cost of the freeway and its relation to the time saved should be weighed against the social cost of building.
Questioned why the noise measurements were taken during a period when Northwest Airlines were on strike and the eastwest runway was shut down for resurfacing.
Questioned the 70.8 dBA and 71.3 dBA measurements with the Airport Spur and and the Airport Spur with ramps at Howell Avenue respectively which were already 1.3 dBA over the federal noise standards and will increase with the spur and normal aircraft traffic.
The School Board took a noise study at Hamlin-Garland School that produced noise levels higher than the readings in the Draft EIS.
The School Board study indicated that hearing damage can occur if noise persists for a long time.
g) Please see responses No. 3 & 4 to statement I on page 181.
This Final EIS considers not only the social impact of building the Airport Spur but also the environmental and economic impacts.
See page 121 for a response.
These figures were not measured values but rather 1990 predicted noise levels with both I-94 and Airport Spur traffic included. These figures were not contained in the Draft EIS but were contained in the September 12, 1973 letter from Milwaukee County Expressway and Transportation Director to their Commission and are incoporated in the Final EIS.
